prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a close-range indoor tabletop scene where the camera wearer's hands holding playing cards at the bottom center and a mug at the bottom left are brightest and nearest (about 0.3 to 0.5 metres away, within the wearer's arm's reach). Just behind the mug on the left side of the glass coffee table (about 0.6 to 1.0 metres away, within reach of both people) sit a tall textured vase, three water bottles, and a soda can arranged within 0.1 to 0.2 metres of each other, while a second teal mug rests near the back-right corner of the table around 1.0 to 1.2 metres out. On the right side at roughly 0.7 to 1.2 metres, another seated person's legs, torso, and arms face leftward and slightly toward the camera wearer, with their head cropped out of the upper-right frame edge so gaze cannot be directly observed. Across frames 1 to 4 the spatial layout stays nearly static as the wearer fans the cards, whereas in frame 5 the camera turns down and rightward while the wearer's right arm extends forward to hand a stack of cards directly into the other person's reaching hands at roughly 0.5 to 0.7 metres. The depth map clarifies the continuous distance gradient across the transparent glass tabletop and separates the foreground cards and outstretched hand from the table surface below better than RGB alone, but it is unreliable on the background shelving beyond 2 metres (which collapses into black) and flattens the internal geometry of the specular vase and transparent bottles.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground objects and people on and around the table: a foreground cup at the bottom left (0.4 metres), a tall vase on the upper left (0.6 metres), a tight cluster of three bottles and a soda can (0.7 to 0.9 metres, partially occluding one another from front to back), a farther cup near the top center-right (1.1 metres), and a seated person on the right (0.7 to 1.2 metres) facing toward the left and the camera wearer. The foreground cup and cards are within the camera wearer's immediate reach, while the second cup and right-side table edge are within the seated person's arm's reach, and the person's head and upper shoulders remain out of view beyond the top-right border across all five frames. From frames 1 to 4 the segmented regions remain in stable positions, then in frame 5 the camera rotates rightward and downward, shifting the bottles and cups to the left, cropping out the tall vase, and bringing the camera wearer's extended right arm into the lower-right foreground as a separate person mask overlapping the seated person's hands at 0.5 to 0.7 metres. This map makes the overlapping boundaries among the tightly packed bottles and soda can much easier to distinguish than in the reflective RGB image, and clearly separates the two participants' bodies during the frame 5 handoff. However, it is unreliable in class labeling and temporal consistency: it misses the glass coffee table entirely, misclassifies the decorative vase and background shelving clutter as 'potted plant', labels the soda can as a 'bottle', flickers the foreground mug to 'bowl' in frame 3, and mislabels the held playing cards as 'cake' in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background solely for the seated person on the right side of the scene, located roughly 0.7 to 1.2 metres from the camera wearer and about 0.5 metres to the right of the bottle cluster. In frame 1, yellow torso and left-arm segments together with magenta left and right hand skeletons show the person seated with shoulders angled toward the left and facing the camera wearer's table area, with both hands resting near their lap within arm's reach of the table's right edge while their head and neck are out of view above the frame. Across frames 1 to 4, the person's hands remain hovering in almost the same position with slight finger curl adjustments, and in frame 5—as the camera pans right and tilts down—their left hand skeleton shifts upward and leftward in the frame to meet the camera wearer's reaching hand at about 0.6 metres. The magenta hand skeletons expose fine finger articulation and palm orientation of the seated person's dark-sleeved, shadowed hands that are difficult to resolve in the RGB frames. However, the map is highly incomplete and unreliable for full-scene understanding: it drops the yellow body and arm skeleton entirely after frame 1, fails to detect the person's right hand in frames 2, 3, and 5, and completely misses the camera wearer's own hands in the foreground across all five frames.
